brief: A four-standard-deviation September payrolls beat, with wage growth still slowing, pushes September Fed rate-hike odds back near recent highs even though it is not a smoking gun for hiking. Bloomberg Intelligence's Childe-Freeman expects a short-term dollar lift that fades into the fourth quarter absent a signal of aggressive tightening. JPMorgan's matrix implies a 0.5-1.25% S&P drop, more than options priced in; the dollar jump drags gold lower. Natixis's Hodge says doves need roughly 20bps of disinflation in next week's CPI or the Fed hikes; BlackRock's Rosenberg ties the September 16 decision entirely to that CPI print; BMO and Fitch say the data supports hawks without clinching a hike. Fed officials Warsh and Waller signal labor is fine but inflation, not payrolls, decides the meeting, so event risk has shifted to CPI. Academy Securities' Tchir shows annualized inflation decelerating from 3.3% to 2.4% and Truflation core at 1.3%, notes an Iran-energy argument against hiking despite a limited US strike on Iranian launchers, rules out any cut, and personally expects no hike this year, trading 2-year notes and reducing risk around WIRP levels.
